question.problem:
Consider the solid enclosed between the paraboloids $z=-7+3{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}$ and $z=1+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2},$ whose volume can be written in terms of double integrals, as follows:

$$
V={\int }_{-2}^{2}{\int }_{a(x)}^{b(x)}\,f(x,y)\,dy\,dx
$$

What is ${a}^{2}+{b}^{2}+f?$
question.worked_solution:
First, we need to determine the projection of the intersection of our surfaces onto the $xy$-plane. So, let's find where they intersect.

$$
\begin{aligned}-7+3{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2} & =1+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2} \\ 2{x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & =8\end{aligned}
$$

So, the projection of the intersection in the $xy$-plane is an ellipse.

Notice that our solid can be written as a type I region: 

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,y)\in D,\,\,-7+3{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}\le z\le 1+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}},
$$

where $D$ is the interior of the ellipse $2{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=8.$ 

As a result, the volume of $R$ is given by 

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{-7+3{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}}^{1+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\text{d}z]\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(1+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2})-(-7+3{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}8-2{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the boundary of $D$ consists of 

- the lower part $y=-\sqrt{8-2{x}^{2}},$ and

- the upper part $y=\sqrt{8-2{x}^{2}},$

for $-2\le x\le 2.$ 

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}8-2{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{-2}^{2}{\int }_{-\sqrt{8-2{x}^{2}}}^{\sqrt{8-2{x}^{2}}}\,8-2{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}\,dy\,dx.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}^{2}+{b}^{2}+f & ={(-\sqrt{8-2{x}^{2}})}^{2}+{(\sqrt{8-2{x}^{2}})}^{2}+(8-2{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}) \\  & =(8-2{x}^{2})+(8-2{x}^{2})+(8-2{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}) \\  & =24-6{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
